newsitem.title: USA: Warm weather advances plantings in North Carolina.
newsitem.headline: Warm weather advances plantings in North Carolina.

text.p: Temperatures returned to more seasonable levels in North Carolina during the week ended Sunday and crop plantings advanced as a result, the state's agricultural statistics service said in its weekly crop update.

Soybeans were 68 percent planted, up from 55 percent a week earlier and down from a five-year average of 72 percent. Tobacco (burley) was 80 percent planted, up from 65 percent last week but behind the average of 93 percent.
Soybeans were rated 75 percent good to excellent, 22 percent fair and three percent poor.
Sorghum was 78 percent planted, ahead of the average pace of 73 percent.
Winter wheat harvesting was 60 percent complete, up sharply from last week's 24 percent and the average of 48 percent.
Wheat was rated 74 percent good to excellent, 22 percent fair and four percent poor, the report said.
